I'm thinking through the design for a thread-safe, high-performance in-memory cache in Rust that needs to handle TTL expiration and LRU eviction. The main challenges are balancing thread safety with performance to avoid lock contention, while also tracking entry lifetimes and access patterns to know when to evict items.

I'm considering sharded locks as the best approach—dividing the keyspace into multiple independent shards, each protected by its own lock, which is what high-performance caches like dashmap and Caffeine use. For the LRU tracking, I'll use an arena-based approach with indices instead of trying to manage doubly-linked lists directly in Rust, since that avoids ownership issues. Each shard will contain a HashMap for key lookups, a slab of nodes with prev/next indices for the LRU chain, and head/tail pointers to track the order. For TTL, I'll store expiration times per entry and use lazy expiration on access, with an optional background thread for proactive cleanup.

One issue I'm realizing: with RwLock, reads still need write access to update the LRU position, which defeats the purpose of having a read lock. I'll use parking_lot::Mutex per shard instead for better performance and simpler semantics. I should also mention TinyLFU as an advanced alternative that approximates access patterns without requiring writes on every read.

Now I'll write out a complete, working implementation with the key methods like `new`, `get`, and `insert`.

Writing the Rust implementation... Implementing the shard structure with LRU list operations... Finishing the insert method by attaching the new node to the front and updating the map. Then I'm implementing removal operations—both by index and by key—along with an LRU eviction function that removes the least recently used item. I'm also adding a purge method that scans all nodes and removes any that have expired based on the current time.

Now I'm completing the shard implementation with a length method, then moving to the main Cache struct which wraps multiple shards behind mutexes for thread-safe concurrent access. I'm setting up the constructor to accept a capacity and optional default TTL, with logic to distribute capacity evenly across shards. The hasher is initialized for consistent key distribution across shards.

Implementing the core cache operations now...
